newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Chinese demand for electicity seen doubling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Chinese demand for electicity seen doubling.

text.p: China's demand for electricity is projected to increase 2/1-2 times by the year 2010, Australia's chief commodities forecasting agency said on Monday.

Other developing economies of Asia are expected to show similar growth, Brian Fisher, executive director of the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE), told a meeting of Asian energy ministers in Sydney.
In most of the countries where energy growth is highest, coal is expected to be an important fuel choice for the power sector, Fisher said.

Of a projected additional 435 gigawatts of new coal fired capacity slated to come on stream in the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) region by 2010, nearly 300 gigawatts will be in China, Fisher said.
Traditional coal producers and exporters in the APEC region, Australia, Canada and the United States, are all forecast to increase their exports over the next 14 years, Fisher said.
However, the largest export growth is likely to come from China and Indonesia, he said.
"Both countries are currently large producers of coal with sufficient reserves to permit considerable increases in output," Fisher said.
"The export gains in these countries are likely to derive from productivity improvements in the coal sector, leading to lower costs relative to their major trading partners."
China is also forecast to increase its imports of coal, although to a lesser extent than exports, Fisher said.
"Most of the imports are likely to be in the south eastern coastal zone, which is experiencing rapid economic growth based on a dynamic export-oreiented manufacturing sector," he said.
This is increassing the need to provide secure and sustainable supplies of coal for electricity generation at competitive prices, Fisher said
